text:
AccuKnox Inc. releases Guard 1.1, an Apache-2.0 guardrail for agent inputs and prompt injection
A 4.5B guard fine-tuned from a Qwen3.5-4B base that returns a block probability. The card reports 0.802 on a 27,416-item safety set.

AccuKnox Inc. published Guard 1.1 on Hugging Face on 16 October 2026, by repository creation date. The card describes a guardrail for AI agents that estimates whether an input should be blocked before it reaches the agent, including harmful requests, jailbreaks and prompt injections hidden in documents, emails or tool outputs. It can also rate whether an assistant response is unsafe. Each answer is a probability, with a default block threshold of 0.5.

AI Singapore releases Gemma-SEA-LION-Guard v2, MIT-licensed safety models for Southeast Asian languages
A 31B decision model (plus E4B and E2B) for content moderation and action governance across eight languages. Scores AUPRC 93.5 on general safety.

AI Singapore's AI Products Pillar, funded by the National Research Foundation Singapore, published Gemma-SEA-LION-Guard-v2 in October 2026. The 31B repository was created on 11 October, with E2B and E4B variants following; the card page shows "Last updated: 2026-10-21" and no release date. The 31B card calls it a safety decision model that outputs probability scores rather than free-form text, for content moderation and action governance.

Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri 1, a 78B German and English reasoning MoE under Apache 2.0
Kolibri 1 is a 78B mixture-of-experts reasoning model with 3.46B active parameters, tuned for German and English, under Apache 2.0.

Aleph Alpha published Kolibri 1, a mixture-of-experts reasoning model focused on German and English. The card gives 78.1B total parameters, 3.46B active per token, 50 layers, and 384 experts per layer with one shared and six routed. Context is 1,048,576 tokens, with 262,144 recommended for serving. It supports an explicit reasoning mode and tool calling.

Qwen releases Qwen3-TTS, Apache 2.0 voice cloning in 10 languages
Qwen3-TTS is a family of open TTS models, 0.6B and 1.7B, with 3-second voice cloning, voice design and streaming, under Apache 2.0.

Alibaba's Qwen team released Qwen3-TTS, a family of open text-to-speech checkpoints. The card for the 1.7B Base model lists Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Russian, Portuguese, Spanish and Italian. The Base model clones a voice from "a 3-second rapid voice clone" of reference audio, plus an optional transcript. Sibling checkpoints cover a 1.7B VoiceDesign model, 1.7B and 0.6B CustomVoice models with nine preset timbres, a 0.6B Base model and a tokenizer.

Ai2 releases Olmo 3, with a fully documented 32B Think model under Apache 2.0
Olmo 3 has 7B and 32B Instruct and Think variants. Ai2 releases code, checkpoints and training details alongside the weights.

Ai2 published Olmo 3, a family of 7B and 32B models in Instruct and Think variants. The Hugging Face card here is for Olmo 3 32B Think. The card says long chain-of-thought thinking improves reasoning on math and coding tasks.

Amazon publishes Strands Decider 2B, a small decision model for agent workflows
A 2B LoRA on Qwen3.5-2B-Base, Apache-2.0, with a /v1/systemone server. The card reports 0.779 on 231 public JevBench tasks.

Amazon published strands-decider-2B-qwen3.5-v1-2610 on Hugging Face on 9 October 2026. The card calls it a small, fast decision model for agentic AI. It answers three question types: yes/no, one of N options, and a level on an ordered scale. Each answer carries a calibrated confidence. It is not a text generator.

Boson AI releases Higgs TTS 3, a 4B zero-shot voice cloning model for 100+ languages
Higgs TTS 3 is a roughly 4B voice-cloning TTS with inline control tags and 100+ languages; research and non-commercial licence.

Boson AI released Higgs TTS 3, described as a roughly 4B autoregressive decoder, though file metadata lists 5B. The card claims 100+ languages and reports single-digit error rates on 102 languages: 85 under 5 and 17 between 5 and 10. It offers zero-shot voice cloning, which works better with a reference transcript, and inline tags for emotion, style, prosody and sound effects. Output is 24 kHz, 25 fps with 8 codebooks and an 8,192-token context. Serving is through SGLang-Omni, vLLM-Omni or Boson AI's API.

BreezeBlue releases Breeze-TTS-2, a 3B English and Chinese TTS, non-commercial
Breeze-TTS-2 is a roughly 3B bilingual TTS with cloning, voice design and streaming; weights under a non-commercial licence.

BreezeBlue released the weights and PyTorch inference code for Breeze-TTS-2 on 25 August 2026, per its card. It is an open-weight model of about 3B parameters covering English and Chinese in one model. The card lists Voice Clone (reference audio plus exact transcript), Voice Design from a text description, Voice Direction for steering tone and pace while cloning, inline vocal events such as "(laugh)", and a streaming API returning 24 kHz mono PCM.

An independent developer releases Jev-Style 2B Decision v3, a 2B model with a free hosted API
Apache-2.0 fine-tune of Qwen3.5-2B. The card reports 73.6% on public JevBench items against Jev 1.13 at 86.6%.

A Hugging Face user, chaoliang yan, published Jev-Style-2B-Decision-v3 on 27 September 2026, by repository creation date. The card calls it an independent project, not affiliated with TypeSafe AI, Jev, Laya or the Qwen team. It is a 2B decision model: give it a state and typed questions (choice, yes/no or score) and it returns a calibrated probability for each option in one pass. It does not generate text or take actions.

Convai Innovations releases laya-typed-decisions, a 0.4B ModernBERT decision model
An Apache-2.0 encoder fine-tuned on four synthetic workflows. The card reports 0.766 accuracy and warns its probabilities are over-confident.

Convai Innovations published laya-typed-decisions on Hugging Face on 18 September 2026, by repository creation date. The card calls it a non-autoregressive System 1 decision model for text classification, part of the Laya family. It is fine-tuned on four synthetic workflows: agent-trace observability, customer service, invoice processing and security incidents.

REAX 1.1: a 27B decision model fine-tuned from pplx-decider
Apache-2.0 weights built on REAX 1, itself a fine-tune of pplx-decider-v1.2. The card reports 71.27 on its own SN92 scoring.

REAX published REAX 1.1 on Hugging Face on 21 October 2026, by repository creation date. The card describes a 27B decision model that reads a state and several questions in one forward pass and returns calibrated probabilities without generating text. The maker says it is not affiliated with Perplexity AI or the Qwen team.

decisionmodels releases s1-llm-auto-router, a 183 MB CPU router under MIT
A pruned mmBERT-small that answers seven routing questions in one CPU pass. The card reports 0.898 category accuracy on its held-out set.

The Hugging Face account decisionmodels published s1-llm-auto-router on Hugging Face on 15 October 2026, by repository creation date. The card describes a decision model fine-tuned to classify a request to an LLM before you route it. It answers seven questions in one CPU pass: category, difficulty, stakes, and four yes/no flags for tools, vision, long context and follow-up.

DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash, a multimodal MoE with a much smaller KV cache, under MIT
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is a 552B-backbone multimodal MoE with 1M-token context and a 890-byte-per-token KV cache, under MIT.
DeepSeek published DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. The card describes a multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 552B backbone parameters, 1M-token context, and native image and text input.

distil labs releases an invoice-decision model that approves or holds vendor invoices
A 4B Qwen3.5 fine-tune returning one of five decisions. The card reports 98 of 100 correct on synthetic test invoices.

distil labs published distil-qwen3.5-4b-invoice-decision on Hugging Face on 21 September 2026, by repository creation date. The card describes a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B that checks vendor invoices against the purchase order and goods receipt. It reasons through four checks and returns one of five decisions: approve, hold_no_po, hold_quantity, hold_price or hold_total.

Soprano-80M: an 80M Apache 2.0 TTS that claims 2000x real time on GPU
Soprano-80M is a tiny English-only TTS with under 15 ms streaming latency on GPU, no cloning, Apache 2.0; superseded by Soprano 1.1.

Soprano-80M is an English-only text-to-speech model of about 80M parameters, published under the name Eugene Kwek on Hugging Face. The card gives 22 December 2025 as its release date. It claims up to 2000 times real time on GPU and 20 times real time on CPU, streaming latency under 15 ms on GPU and under 250 ms on CPU, under 1 GB of memory, and 32 kHz output. It runs on CUDA, CPU and MPS on Windows, Linux and macOS, with a WebUI, CLI, Python API and OpenAI-compatible endpoint, though the endpoint is non-streaming only.

Fish Audio releases Drama 3, a 35B mixture-of-experts TTS for multi-character scenes
Drama 3 is a 35B MoE speech model (3B active) with up to 16 speaker tags and voice cloning; research licence.

Fish Audio published Drama 3, which its card describes as a text-to-speech model "built for multi-character scenes and long-form content". The model is 35B parameters in total with 3B active per token, using a mixture-of-experts text backbone. The metadata lists 83 languages. Text can carry speaker tags from <|speaker:0|> to <|speaker:15|>, so up to 16 characters in one script, plus inline tags such as [sighs] and [laughs]. Voice cloning uses a short reference clip with a transcript, and long text is chunked automatically.

Fish Audio releases S2 Pro, a 5B TTS model for 80+ languages, research licence
S2 Pro is a dual-autoregressive TTS model with inline emotion tags; weights are free for research, commercial use needs a licence.

Fish Audio released S2 Pro, a text-to-speech model with a roughly 4B slow autoregressive stage and a 400M fast stage, listed at 5B parameters. The card says it supports 80+ languages, with Japanese, English and Chinese in the top tier. Inline tags such as [tag] take free-form descriptions of prosody and emotion, and the card claims over 15,000 unique tags. It says training used over 10 million hours of audio with reinforcement learning alignment.

FunAudioLLM releases Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512, an Apache 2.0 voice cloning TTS
Fun-CosyVoice3 is a 0.5B zero-shot cloning TTS for nine languages and 18+ Chinese dialects, with latency down to 150 ms.

FunAudioLLM published Fun-CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512, a 0.5B-parameter text-to-speech model. The card dates the 2512 base and RL models to December 2025. It supports nine languages: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, Spanish, French, Italian and Russian, plus 18-plus Chinese dialects and accents. Features include zero-shot multilingual and cross-lingual voice cloning, pronunciation control with Pinyin and English CMU phonemes, instruction control for emotion, speed and volume, and bi-streaming with latency as low as 150 ms.

Google DeepMind releases Gemma 4, with a 31B dense model under Apache 2.0
Gemma 4 comes in five sizes from E2B to 31B, with multimodal input, 256K context on the larger models and an Apache 2.0 licence.

Google DeepMind published Gemma 4, a family of open models. The card for the 31B instruction-tuned model lists five sizes: E2B, E4B, 12B, 26B A4B and 31B. The family handles text and image input, with audio on the E2B, E4B and 12B models, and generates text. Context is up to 256K tokens on the medium models and 128K on the small ones, with support for over 140 languages.

H2O.ai releases H2O Lightning 4B, an Apache-2.0 decision model with GGUF builds
Built on Qwen3.5-4B, with GGUF files from 1.43 GB for llama.cpp. The card reports 88.74% on 231 public JevBench text questions.

H2O.ai published h2o-lightning-4b on Hugging Face on 2 October 2026, by repository creation date. The GGUF repository is the llama.cpp packaging of it. The card describes a decision model that answers typed decisions with probabilities: named choice options, true/false questions and ordered score levels. It serves decisions through a /v1/systemone endpoint.

Hume AI releases TADA-1B, an English TTS that aligns one speech vector per text token
TADA-1B is Hume AI's open English TTS built on Llama 3.2 1B, with 1:1 text-to-speech alignment; Llama 3.2 licence.

Hume AI published TADA-1B, an English text-to-speech model built on Llama 3.2 1B. The Hub lists it at 2B parameters in BF16, though the name says 1B. The card describes 1:1 alignment, where the tokenizer produces one speech vector per text token, which it says removes the need for fixed-frame-rate processing, and dual-stream generation that produces a text token and the preceding token's speech together. Speech continuation is supported through a num_extra_steps setting.

IBM releases Granite 4.1 8B, an Apache 2.0 instruct model for enterprise tasks
Granite 4.1 8B is a long-context instruct model with better tool calling and instruction following, under Apache 2.0.

IBM released Granite-4.1-8B, an 8B-parameter long-context instruct model fine-tuned from Granite-4.1-8B-Base. The card gives a release date of April 29th, 2026 and credits the Granite Team at IBM. It says Granite 4.1 went through an improved post-training pipeline, including supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning alignment, that improves tool calling, instruction following and chat.

IBM releases Granite Guardian 4.1 8B, a judge model for safety, RAG and agent checks
Apache-2.0 judge on Granite 4.1 8B with a hybrid reasoning mode. Covers harm, groundedness and function-calling hallucination, plus custom criteria.

IBM Research released Granite Guardian 4.1 8B in April 2026; the Hugging Face repository was created on 16 April. It is a safety model that judges whether prompts or responses meet specified criteria, with a hybrid mode that can reason before scoring or return a direct yes/no. It is fine-tuned from Granite 4.1 8B, has 8B parameters and is licensed Apache-2.0.

Shanghai AI Laboratory releases Intern-Decision, multimodal decision models from 0.8B to 4B
Intern-Decision-4B is fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-4B and answers up to 16 questions per pass, with image input. Apache-2.0.

Shanghai AI Laboratory published the Intern-Decision family on Hugging Face in late September 2026. The 4B repository was created on 26 September; the card gives no release date, so that is the date used here. Sizes visible on the Hub include 0.8B, 2B and 4B.

Jared Palmer releases Kev-9B, an Apache-2.0 LoRA decision model on Qwen3.5-9B
An independent adapter that implements TypeSafe's System One API. The card reports 0.852 on a locked out-of-domain test.

Jared Palmer published Kev-9B on Hugging Face on 20 September 2026, by repository creation date. The card describes a decision model that reads one document and a set of typed questions and returns calibrated probabilities over the supplied options in a single forward pass, without generating text. It implements TypeSafe's System One API.

JetBrains releases Mellum2.1 Thinking, a 12B coding MoE with 2.5B active, under Apache 2.0
Mellum2.1 Thinking is a 12B mixture-of-experts reasoning model with 2.5B active, retrained mostly with reinforcement learning on real repositories.

JetBrains published Mellum2.1 Thinking, the next version of Mellum2 Thinking. The architecture is unchanged: 12B total and 2.5B active parameters, 28 layers, 64 experts with 8 active, and a 131,072-token context. Almost all the new work went into post-training, where reinforcement learning became the main stage of training.

k2-fsa releases OmniVoice, a 0.6B zero-shot TTS covering 600+ languages
OmniVoice is a 0.6B voice-cloning and voice-design TTS tagged for 646 languages; code Apache 2.0, weights CC-BY-NC.

k2-fsa released OmniVoice, a 0.6B-parameter text-to-speech model with Qwen3-0.6B-Base as its base. The card says it covers over 600 languages and carries a 646-language tag. It offers zero-shot voice cloning from short reference audio, voice design from attributes such as gender, age, pitch, accent and whisper, non-verbal symbols such as laughter tags, and pronunciation correction through pinyin or phonemes. Output is 24 kHz audio.

Katanemo releases Arch-Router 1.5B, a router that follows your own route descriptions
For context: a Qwen2.5-1.5B-based model that maps a query to a user-defined route and returns JSON. Released under the Katanemo licence.

For context: Arch-Router is from mid-2025, outside the last twelve months, and is included as an early open router model. The card cites a paper, arXiv 2506.16655, published on 19 June 2025. The Hub repository was created on 30 May 2025.

Liquid AI releases LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24B on-device reasoning MoE with 2B active
LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-parameter reasoning model with about 2.45B active, built for agents on-device, under the LFM1.0 licence.

Liquid AI published LFM2.5-24B-A2B, which the card calls the largest and final model in the LFM2.5 family. It is a text-only reasoning model with 24.0B total and 2.45B active parameters, 40 layers (30 double-gated short convolution blocks and 10 grouped-query attention blocks) and 64 experts per MoE block with top-4 routing. Context is 131,072 tokens. It covers 16 languages, listed on the card.

Maincode releases Matilda Decision v1, a 27B multimodal decision model
Apache-2.0 weights on Qwen3.8-27B. The maker's own run scores 65.38 on the public Jev Decision Index 0.3 suite.

Maincode published Matilda Decision v1 on Hugging Face on 15 October 2026, by repository creation date. The card describes a 27B multimodal decision model that takes text or JSON, optionally with images, and answers several questions in one call. It returns a probability for each answer and generates no text. Question types are multiple choice up to 255 options, yes/no and rating.

Meta releases Llama Guard 4, a 12B multimodal safety classifier
For context: a dense 12B pruned from Llama 4 Scout that screens prompts and responses across 14 MLCommons hazard categories. Gated under the Llama 4 licence.

For context: Llama Guard 4 is from April 2025, outside the last twelve months, and is included because it defines the category. The card gives the licence effective date as 5 April 2025 and no exact release date. The Hub repository was created on 23 April 2025.

Microsoft releases Decision-1, a 9B model that scores fixed answer options
Microsoft-Decision-1 returns a probability per answer option instead of prose. Hosted on Foundry and OpenRouter; no licence stated.

Microsoft announced Microsoft-Decision-1 on 9 October 2026. It is a text-only decision-scoring model post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B. You give it evidence, a closed question and a fixed set of answer options. It returns a probability for each option in one pass. It does not write explanations.

Microsoft releases VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B, a streaming TTS model under MIT
A single-speaker streaming TTS model that starts speaking in about 300 ms; MIT licensed, but the card says research use only.

Microsoft published VibeVoice-Realtime-0.5B, a text-to-speech model built on a Qwen2.5-0.5B language model. The card says it takes streaming text input and produces first audible speech in about 300 ms, depending on hardware. It uses an acoustic tokenizer at 7.5 Hz with no semantic tokenizer, and a diffusion head conditioned on the language model's hidden states. Context is 8k tokens, with generation of about 10 minutes.

Mistral AI releases Shieldstral 1.0, a 3B multimodal safety classifier under Apache 2.0
Shieldstral judges text or images against a policy you write and returns an unsafe score. Reported best F1 on several benchmarks; Apache-2.0.

Mistral AI released Shieldstral 1.0 3B. The Hugging Face repository was created on 16 July 2026 and the card lists an accompanying paper published on 28 July. The card carries no release date, so the repository date is used. It is a safety classifier that judges text, images or both against a natural-language policy and returns a continuous unsafe score.

Mistral releases Voxtral TTS, a 4B open-weights speech model, non-commercial
Voxtral 4B TTS covers nine languages with 20 preset voices and streaming; weights are CC BY-NC 4.0.

Mistral AI released Voxtral 4B TTS (2603), described on its card as "a frontier, open-weights text-to-speech model" for voice agents. It supports nine languages: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Arabic and Hindi. It ships with 20 preset voices and the card mentions "easy adaptation to new voices" through AI Studio. The card does not use the term voice cloning. Output is 24 kHz audio in several formats, with streaming and batch inference. The base model is Ministral-3-3B-Base-2512.

Mistral releases Ministral 3, edge models in 3B, 8B and 14B under Apache 2.0
Ministral 3 is a family of 3B, 8B and 14B edge models with vision, in base, instruct and reasoning versions, under Apache 2.0.

Mistral AI published Ministral 3, a family of edge models. The repository names show 3B, 8B and 14B sizes, each with base, instruct and reasoning variants. This item uses the card for Ministral 3 14B Instruct 2512, which the card calls the largest of the family and says is comparable in performance to the larger Mistral Small 3.2 24B.

Mistral releases Medium 3.5, a dense 128B model with a modified MIT licence
Mistral Medium 3.5 is a dense 128B instruct, reasoning and coding model with 256k context. The licence excludes large-revenue companies.

Mistral AI published Mistral Medium 3.5 on Hugging Face. The card calls it the company's first flagship merged model: a dense 128B model with a 256k context window that handles instruction following, reasoning and coding in one set of weights. It replaces Mistral Medium 3.1 and Magistral in Le Chat and Devstral 2 in the Vibe coding agent.

Moonshot releases Kimi K2 Thinking, a 1T MoE thinking agent with native INT4
Kimi K2 Thinking is a 1T-parameter MoE with 32B active, 256K context and native INT4 quantisation, under a modified MIT licence.

The moonshotai organisation published Kimi K2 Thinking, which its card calls the latest and most capable open-source thinking model in the line. It is built as a thinking agent that reasons step by step while calling tools. The card claims stable behaviour across 200 to 300 sequential tool calls.

Moonshot releases Kimi K3, a 2.8T-parameter open-weights multimodal model
Kimi K3 is a 2.8T mixture-of-experts model with 104B active parameters and 1M-token context, under the Kimi K3 License.

The moonshotai organisation published Kimi K3 on Hugging Face. The card calls it an open-weight, native multimodal agentic model with 2.8 trillion parameters, 104 billion of them activated per token. It takes text, images and video and supports a 1-million-token context.

Nari Labs releases Dia2-2B, a streaming English dialogue TTS under Apache 2.0
Dia2-2B is a 2B English dialogue TTS that can start speaking before the full text arrives; Apache 2.0, about two minutes max.

Nari Labs published Dia2-2B, a 2B-parameter English text-to-speech model for dialogue. The card says generation can start once the first few words of text are provided, which suits streaming into speech-to-speech systems. Multi-speaker scripts use [S1] and [S2] tags, audio can be conditioned on speaker prefix clips, and word timestamps are available relative to the Mimi codec's roughly 12.5 Hz frame rate. It runs through a CLI, a Python API and a Gradio app, and needs uv and CUDA 12.8 or newer drivers.

NineNineSix releases KaniTTS2-en, a 400M English TTS with voice cloning
KaniTTS2-en is a 400M English TTS on LFM2 350M with cloning via a speaker embedder, about 3 GB VRAM; LFM 1.0 licence.

NineNineSix published KaniTTS2-en, an English text-to-speech model of 400M parameters on a LiquidAI LFM2 350M backbone. The card describes a two-stage pipeline pairing the language model with an FSQ audio codec (Nvidia NanoCodec), 22 kHz output, and voice cloning through a speaker embedder. It is aimed at real-time conversation.

NVIDIA releases MagpieTTS Multilingual 357M v2607, 12 languages with preset voices
MagpieTTS Multilingual 357M v2607 covers 12 languages with five preset voices; voice cloning was removed. NVIDIA Open Model License.

NVIDIA's MagpieTTS Multilingual 357M reached version v2607 on 21 July 2026, per the model card, after earlier tags v2602 (March 2026) and v2512 (January 2026). It is a 364M-parameter encoder-decoder transformer covering 12 languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish and Vietnamese. It ships with five preset English speaker voices that speak all 12 languages; four are proprietary and one is public. Output is 22.05 kHz mono.

NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety, a 4B multilingual moderation classifier
Gemma-3-4B-based, 12 languages, text plus one image, with custom-policy mode. Open licence plus Gemma terms; card dated 2 June 2026.

NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety model card is dated 2 June 2026 (version V1.2). It classifies prompts, an optional image and optional responses as safe or unsafe. It has about 4B parameters, is based on Google Gemma-3-4B-it with a LoRA adapter merged back, and uses a SigLIP vision encoder at 896x896.

NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3 Content Safety, a 4B moderation classifier on Gemma-3
Predecessor to 3.5: 4B, 12 languages, 23 safety categories. Released 16 March 2026 under the NVIDIA open model licence plus Gemma terms.

NVIDIA's model card for Nemotron 3 Content Safety gives a release date of 16 March 2026 (version V1.1) and says training ran from October 2025 to March 2026. It is a 4B-parameter LLM classifier that moderates prompts (text plus an optional image) and optional model responses. It returns safe or unsafe and, on request, the violated categories.

NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3 Nano 30B-A3B, a hybrid Mamba-MoE reasoning model
Nemotron 3 Nano is a 30B hybrid Mamba-2 and MoE model with 3.5B active parameters, under the NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License.

NVIDIA published Nemotron 3 Nano 30B-A3B in BF16. The card describes a large language model trained from scratch by NVIDIA as a unified model for reasoning and non-reasoning tasks. It first writes a reasoning trace and then answers, and the trace can be switched off with a flag in the chat template.

OpenAI opens its Decisions API in public beta, built on GPT-6 Luna
A /v1/decisions endpoint returns typed predicate, choice and score answers. Public beta, $0.10 per million input tokens, GA promised in weeks.

OpenAI's Decisions API is a dedicated endpoint, POST /v1/decisions, that evaluates text, images or both and returns typed answers instead of prose. The docs say it is in public beta and expected to reach general availability in the coming weeks. The only supported model is gpt-6-luna.

OpenAI releases gpt-oss-safeguard, open-weight safety reasoning models that read your policy
20b and 120b Apache-2.0 models that classify text against a policy you supply at inference time, with configurable reasoning effort.

For context: this is a late-2025 release that later guard models compare themselves against. The date here, 29 October 2025, is the last-updated date of the Hugging Face collection shown on the model card. The card itself gives no release date, and the repository was created earlier, on 18 September 2025.

OpenBMB releases MiniCPM5-2B, a dense 2B model with open training data, under Apache 2.0
MiniCPM5-2B is a dense 2B on-device model for coding, tool use and long context, released with its UltraData training sets.

OpenBMB published MiniCPM5-2B, the second model in its MiniCPM5 series after MiniCPM5-1B. It is a dense 2B transformer, listed at about 2.5 billion parameters on Hugging Face, aimed at on-device and resource-constrained use. Tags on the card include long-context, tool-calling and edge-ai, and the language list is English and Chinese.

OpenBMB releases VoxCPM2, a 2B Apache 2.0 TTS with voice design and 48 kHz output
VoxCPM2 is a 2B tokenizer-free TTS covering 30 languages, with voice design, cloning and 48 kHz output, under Apache 2.0.

OpenBMB released VoxCPM2, a 2B-parameter text-to-speech model built on the MiniCPM-4 backbone with a tokenizer-free diffusion autoregressive design. The card lists 30 languages that need no language tag, plus nine Chinese dialects. It accepts 16 kHz reference audio and outputs 48 kHz.

OpenMOSS Team releases MOSS-TTS, an 8B Apache 2.0 voice cloning and long-form TTS
MOSS-TTS is an 8B (and 1.7B) open TTS family with cloning, up to an hour of long-form audio and duration control.

OpenMOSS Team released MOSS-TTS, a family led by an 8B flagship (MossTTSDelay, recommended for production) and a 1.7B MossTTSLocal (recommended for research). The card lists 20 languages but its table shows 19. Features include zero-shot voice cloning from reference audio, long-form generation described as up to one hour in a single run, token-level duration control (about 12.5 audio tokens per second), Pinyin and IPA pronunciation input, and code-switching within one utterance. Siblings include MOSS-TTSD for dialogue, MOSS-VoiceGenerator for voice design, MOSS-SoundEffect and MOSS-TTS-Realtime, which reports 180 ms time to first byte.

Perplexity releases pplx-decider, an Apache-2.0 27B decision model
pplx-decider-v1 and v1.1 are open-weight 27B models that return probabilities for fixed answers. Built on Qwen3.8-27B.

Perplexity published pplx-decider-v1-27b on Hugging Face on 1 October 2026 and pplx-decider-v1.1-27b on 5 October, by repository creation date. Both are open-weight decision models under Apache-2.0. Given a state and questions, they return probabilities for the answers rather than text.

Policies
How Shipped decides what to list, how it marks and scores items, what counts as evidence, and how we handle corrections, disclosure and readers.
How the Shipped desk works. These are the rules we apply to every item. Sections marked as coming are not live yet.

Decision4Rec releases Kev models that rerank recommender candidates
Apache-2.0 adapters from 0.8B to 27B that read a pool of 30 candidates and output a probability for each. Development results only.

Marco Polignano and co-authors published decision4rec-kev-9b on Hugging Face on 19 October 2026, by repository creation date. Sibling repositories at 0.8B, 4B and 27B appear on the Hub. The card describes a decision model for recommender systems. It reads the 30 best candidates from a multi-agent pool, with item text, knowledge-graph statements and the agents that found each candidate, then outputs one probability per candidate in a single forward pass.

Qwen releases Qwen3.8-27B, a dense 27B vision-language model under Apache 2.0
Qwen3.8-27B is a dense 27B model with a vision encoder, 262,144-token native context and switchable thinking, under Apache 2.0.

Qwen published Qwen3.8-27B, the compact dense member of its Qwen3.8 generation. The card calls Qwen3.8 the most capable generation in the Qwen open-model family to date. It is a causal language model with a vision encoder, so it takes images and video as well as text. The layout mixes Gated DeltaNet and gated attention layers, 64 layers in all.

Qwen releases Qwen3Guard, multilingual moderation models in 0.6B, 4B and 8B
Apache-2.0 safety classifiers covering 119 languages with Safe, Controversial and Unsafe levels; Stream variants are also on the Hub.

For context: Qwen3Guard predates the twelve-month window by a few weeks, and is included because it is a base case for open guard models. The Hugging Face repositories were created on 23 September 2025, and the card cites a technical report published on 16 October 2025.

Reflection releases Beam, a 501B open-weights MoE under Apache 2.0
Beam is Reflection's first open model: 501B total and 23B active parameters, 1M-token context, under Apache 2.0.

Reflection published Beam, an instruction-tuned open model. The card gives 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters across 52 layers with 256 experts, a 1M-token context and text-only input. Weights come in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4. The stated knowledge cutoff is June 30, 2026.

Resemble AI releases Chatterbox-Turbo, a 350M MIT TTS built for voice agents
Chatterbox-Turbo is a 350M English TTS with paralinguistic tags, one-step decoding and voice cloning; MIT licensed and watermarked.

Resemble AI published Chatterbox-Turbo, a 350M-parameter English text-to-speech model aimed mainly at low-latency voice agents, though the card says it also suits narration. The speech-token-to-mel decoder was distilled from 10 generation steps to one, reducing compute and VRAM compared with earlier Chatterbox models. It supports paralinguistic tags such as [cough], [laugh] and [chuckle], and clones a voice from a reference clip; the card's example uses a 10-second clip. Every output carries Resemble's PerTh watermark, which the card describes as imperceptible and surviving MP3 compression.

SberAI releases FRIDA-Decisions, a Russian and English encoder for structured decisions
A 0.8B MIT-licensed encoder that picks, rates, answers yes/no or ranks in one pass. The card reports 0.893 on 735 razvilka items.

SberAI (listed on the card as УЭСМО, SberAI) published FRIDA-Decisions on Hugging Face on 2 October 2026, by repository creation date. The card describes a Russian-language encoder model for structured decisions on text. It picks one option from a set, places text on an ordinal scale, answers yes or no, or ranks candidates, all in a single encoder pass with no text generation.

Skywork releases Reward-V2, eight reward models from 0.6B to 8B
For context: Llama and Qwen3-based preference scorers trained on about 26 million pairs. The 8B card reports 96.4 on RewardBench v1.

For context: this is a mid-2025 release, outside the last twelve months, included because reward models are a core kind of decision model. The card says the paper was published on 2 July 2025 and the collection was last updated on 4 July 2025.

Soul-AILab releases SoulX-Podcast-1.7B, a multi-speaker podcast TTS in English and Chinese
SoulX-Podcast-1.7B generates multi-turn, multi-speaker dialogue with cross-dialect cloning in English and Chinese; Apache 2.0.

Soul-AILab published SoulX-Podcast-1.7B, a text-to-speech model designed for podcast-style multi-turn, multi-speaker dialogue, which also handles conventional monologue. The Hub lists it at 2B parameters in BF16 though the name says 1.7B. It supports English and Chinese plus the Sichuanese, Henanese and Cantonese dialects, the dialect inference using a separate SoulX-Podcast-1.7B-dialect model. Features listed are long-form multi-speaker generation, cross-dialectal zero-shot voice cloning, and paralinguistic controls such as laughter and sighs.

StartLux releases Decision v1.1, from 0.8B to 27B, with non-commercial weights
StartLux-Decision-v1.1 ships Instant and AutoThink variants. Weights are CC BY-NC 4.0; commercial use needs a separate licence.

StartLux published StartLux-Decision v1.1 on Hugging Face in October 2026. The 27B Instant repository was created on 11 October, which is the date used here. The card describes a decision model that takes a state of text or JSON, with up to 8 images, plus typed questions: choice, yes/no and score. It returns a probability for every option in one forward pass. Its request format is compatible with the System One /v1/systemone API.

StepFun releases Step 3.7 Flash, a 198B vision-language MoE with 11B active parameters
Step 3.7 Flash is a 198B sparse MoE vision-language model with about 11B active parameters and 256k context, under Apache 2.0.

StepFun published Step 3.7 Flash. The card describes a 198B-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts vision-language model: a 196B language backbone plus a 1.8B vision encoder, with about 11B parameters active per token. It claims up to 400 tokens per second, a 256k context window and three reasoning levels (low, medium, high).

StepFun releases Step-Audio-EditX, a 3B open-weights model for editing and generating speech
A 3B model that edits emotion and style in speech and does zero-shot text-to-speech. Weights and code are public; the weights licence is not stated.

StepFun released the weights and inference code for Step-Audio-EditX on 12 November 2025. It is a 3B-parameter model that edits emotion, speaking style and paralinguistic sounds in speech, and it also does zero-shot text-to-speech and voice cloning.

Supertone releases Supertonic 3, a 99M on-device TTS in 31 languages
Supertonic 3 is a roughly 99M ONNX TTS for local and browser use across 31 languages; OpenRAIL-M model, MIT sample code.

Supertone released Supertonic 3, a text-to-speech model of about 99M parameters shipped as ONNX assets. The card says it runs locally with ONNX Runtime with no cloud call and no GPU requirement, which suits browser, edge and local use. It supports 31 languages, up from 5 in Supertonic 2, including English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, Hindi and Vietnamese. Expression tags such as laughs, breaths and sighs are supported.

Torchcast AI releases Torchcast Decision 27B, built on StartLux weights
A LoRA fine-tune of StartLux-Decision-27B that speaks the /v1/systemone API. Weights are CC BY-NC 4.0; card reports 65.00 on Index 0.2.1.

Torchcast AI published torchcast-decision-27b on Hugging Face on 3 October 2026, by repository creation date. The card describes a 27B model that answers typed questions about a state: multiple choice, yes/no and ordinal rating. It returns a probability for every option and answers all questions in a request in one forward pass.

TypeSafe AI launches Jev, a hosted model for typed software decisions
Jev takes state and typed questions and returns probabilities. Early access via API, $0.042 per million input tokens; weights not stated.

TypeSafe AI introduced Jev, which it calls its first System One model, in a post dated 15 September 2026. The page metadata shows 19 October, so the date is inconsistent. Jev takes unstructured state and typed questions and returns typed outputs with calibrated probabilities and a confidence estimate. It does not generate free text.

vLLM Semantic Router team releases Decision 2.0 open decision models
Decision 2.0 is an Apache-2.0 family from vllm-sr. The 27B Vega card reports 74.0 on JevArena. Lux is a 9B sibling.

The vLLM Semantic Router team published its Decision 2.0 family on Hugging Face at the end of September 2026. The Vega-27B repository was created on 29 September and the Lux-9B repository the same day. The release date here is the repository creation date, since the card gives no announcement date.

Xiaomi MiMo releases MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL, a 1.02T omnimodal MoE under MIT
MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL is the flagship of the MiMo-V2.6 series: 1.02T total, 42B active, 1M context, text, image, video and audio in.

Xiaomi MiMo published MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL, which the card calls the flagship checkpoint of the MiMo-V2.6 series. It is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 1.02T total and 42B activated parameters, a 1M-token context, and input in text, image, video and audio. It includes a vision encoder and an audio encoder, and a 5-layer multi-token-prediction head for speculative decoding.

Yandex releases AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, an Apache 2.0 base MoE for Russian and English
AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base is an 80B base model with 3B active parameters and 262,144-token context, trained from scratch.

Yandex published AliceAI-Foundation-80B-A3B-Base, a base language model with a hybrid architecture and MoE layers. The card says it has 80B parameters with 3B active per token, 262,144 tokens of context, and was trained entirely from scratch. The layout repeats three KDA plus MoE layers then one gated attention plus MoE layer, for 48 layers, with 512 experts (10 routed and one shared). The languages are Russian and English.

Z.ai releases GLM-TTS, an MIT-licensed Chinese and English voice cloning model
GLM-TTS is an open Chinese-English TTS with 3-10 second voice cloning and reinforcement learning tuning; MIT licensed.

Z.ai published GLM-TTS, a text-to-speech model for Chinese and English, optimised for mixed text. The card describes two stages: a Llama-based language model generates speech tokens, then a flow-matching model produces mel-spectrograms that a vocoder turns into audio. Features include zero-shot voice cloning from 3 to 10 seconds of prompt audio, reinforcement learning (GRPO) with multiple rewards for expressiveness, hybrid phoneme and text input to control pronunciation such as polyphones, and streaming inference. The card does not state a parameter count.

Z.ai releases GLM-5.3, a 753B open-weights model aimed at coding and cyber tasks
GLM-5.3 reuses the GLM-5.2 base with new post-training. The weights are public under a custom glm-5.3 licence.

Z.ai released GLM-5.3 on Hugging Face. The card says it uses the same base model as GLM-5.2, so every gain comes from post-training. The Hugging Face record lists about 753 billion parameters in total.
